standard_prerequisites.name: Weighted Sobolev norm H^{sigma}_M
standard_prerequisites.statement: The norm is the sum over multi-indices of order at most M of the L2 norms of <nabla_k>^sigma (k^alpha g).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the norm appearing on the right-hand side of the statement and reordered twice inside the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: L2 trace lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: For g in H^s(R^d) with s > (d-1)/2 and a straight line C, the L2 norm of g on C is bounded by the H^s norm of g.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied to the directional line at source line 1044 to pass from the one-dimensional integral to a full space integral.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and Plancherel
standard_prerequisites.statement: Standard inequalities converting an integral of |f| into an L2 norm and back between physical and frequency space.
standard_prerequisites.use: Cauchy-Schwarz opens the proof at line 1044 and Plancherel converts back at line 1049.

core_obligations: Bound the directional integral by Cauchy-Schwarz, introducing the weight |s|^{2n+1+2 delta_0} so that the one-dimensional integral becomes an L2 norm along the line (source lines 1044-1046).

Apply the L2 trace lemma to that line and rewrite the resulting full-space integral over k with the weight <nabla_k>^{ceil(d/2)} against |k|^{n+1/2+delta_0} times the derivative of the Fourier transform (source lines 1046-1048).
Apply Plancherel to return to physical space, producing the L2 norm of <x>^{ceil(d/2)} <nabla_x>^{n+1/2+delta_0}(x^alpha g(x)) (source lines 1049-1051).

Bound <x>^{ceil(d/2)} by the sum over |beta| <= ceil(d/2) of |x^beta|, reorder the moments and derivatives with the retained ordering lemma, and recognise the weighted Sobolev norm with index alpha + ceil(d/2) (source lines 1051-1054).

proof_roadmap.step: L2 trace on the direction line and rewriting the full-space integral.
Expand the polynomial weight, reorder moments and derivatives, and read off the norm.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `gnorm` at source lines 1037-1042: the integral over s >= 0 of |s|^n times the absolute value of the alpha-th derivative of the Fourier transform evaluated on the ray s k/|k| is bounded by the weighted Sobolev norm of g of order n + 1/2 + delta_0 and index alpha + ceil(d/2), uniformly in k different from 0. The proof (source lines 1043-1056) is a four-step chain in which each step changes the space being integrated over: Cauchy-Schwarz introduces the half-integral weight 2n+1+2delta_0 that makes the line integral an L2 norm (lines 1044-1046), the L2 trace lemma replaces that norm by a full space integral with the extra weight <nabla_k>^{ceil(d/2)} (lines 1046-1048), Plancherel returns to physical space (lines 1049-1051), and only then do the polynomial weight expansion and the ordering lemma for moments and derivatives bring the expression to the stated weighted Sobolev norm (lines 1051-1054). The statement records the endpoint only.
